title: inbuf_append: each append re-kmallocs entire buffer — quadratic for many small writes
description: inbuf_append() allocates a new buffer of size (inbuf_len + len), copies the existing inbuf, then frees the old one. This is O(n^2) in the number of write() calls: N writes of 1 byte each produce N kmalloc+memcpy+kfree sequences. For a 4KB key across 4096 1-byte writes: 4096 allocations, total bytes copied = 1+2+...+4096 = ~8MB. While key material writes are not expected to be split across many tiny writes, there is no limit on the number of write() calls to an UNSET fd before KEY_IMPORT. A malicious userspace can cause excessive kernel memory allocations. The MAX_PAYLOAD limit (1MB) bounds the total size but not the number of iterations. Each iteration holds two allocations simultaneously (old + new) before freeing old. The total allocation work is O(n^2). This is a minor correctness/efficiency issue — not exploitable for kernel memory exhaustion due to MAX_PAYLOAD limit. Flag as low-priority correctness issue.
